changes: The necklace gate is a connection test. The agents in a necklace were tested already as pearls, so the gate checks that the chain connects and keeps answering, not their accuracy again.

Stage 1 joins the steps one at a time, runs the whole chain, and runs each step once with its representative member left out to see a fallback answer. Stage 2 runs the whole chain three more times on different task inputs; all three must pass.
Every required step has a representative pearl and at least one outside fallback. A step with no outside fallback in the market uses our own agent, approved by its own connection runs.

After opening, one connection run a day keeps a necklace open; it is held when that run fails or is older than 48 hours. When a fallback answers a public run, a task opens to build our own agent for that role.
The earlier held-out answer rounds (57 of 60) are no longer the necklace gate.
A verified pearl needs one KST day on which it scores 85 or more on its role task, accurate and clean, instead of two different days.

Role tests run in 8 windows a day. Each window allows at most 100 new candidates and 20 retests (120 tests; 60 when refusals pass 5%), so a day allows at most 800 new candidates and 160 retests. These are limits, not counts of tests run.

When the evaluator changes, a result whose whole answer was kept is judged again by the new evaluator and counts toward two-day repetition under it; a result without its whole answer is not counted together with the new evaluator’s successes.

A task whose input reaches no parameter of a tool is skipped as cannot fill instead of being called with other values. One earlier pass was wrong for this reason: github.repo 136184 on 2026-11-15 was asked another search, and its first result happened to show the expected license; it no longer counts.
A necklace may open with provisional members: a step can be led by an agent that is not a verified pearl yet, so useful necklaces open without waiting for every pearl.

A verified pearl scored at least the report threshold on two different days; a provisional member scored at least the provisional threshold in one report within the last seven days, or is our own substitute that passed its held-out gate. The numbers come from the judge and are shown in section 5.
A verified pearl takes the place of a provisional member once it is verified.
The answer gate does not change: a necklace opens only after its answers pass the same gate as before.
Each necklace page says, step by step, whether a verified pearl or a member under verification leads it.
Retest rules say what runs: after its gate, a necklace is held at the next daily check when a day’s retest success is below 0.8, a retest is older than 48 hours, or its delta is 0 or less.
The retest pass rate of 0.95 is removed: 0.95 is the gate’s rate for the first opening, and retests do not enforce it.
The page opens with what we measure: real read-only calls judged against known facts, tool-list and answer hashes, and the last successful check.
First public version: candidates, how a test runs, the score out of 100, verified and final pearls, the necklace gate, 32 roles and limits.
Necklace gate values come from the gate's own constants (agent_market/necklaces/gate_rules); held-out answer sets stay withheld.
